elements.text: Phones and sleep  /  Science project, Year 2
Most teenagers sleep less than they need
Doctors recommend 8 to 10 hours for people aged 14 to 17. Surveys in Sweden find that about half of upper secondary students sleep under 7.
Phones are the new suspect. They light up, buzz and pull us back into a conversation we thought we had left.
what our own students averaged before the test

pages.name: Background
pages.notes: Two numbers frame the whole project: what teenagers need and what our class actually gets. The gap is the reason for the study.

elements.text: Phones and sleep  /  Science project, Year 2
Teens with a phone in the bedroom slept 21 minutes less on school nights.
Notifications after bedtime delayed sleep by half an hour in one in four students.
Leaving the phone outside for two weeks added 24 minutes. Self reported only.

pages.name: Hypothesis
pages.notes: A hypothesis has to be something the data could prove wrong. Ours says at least 30 minutes, so a 10 minute difference would count against us.

elements.text: Phones and sleep  /  Science project, Year 2
Two classes, 84 students, split into two groups of 42 by drawing names.
Both groups sleep as usual. Everyone fills in a diary each morning.
Group B leaves the phone in a box in the hallway from 22:00.
We work out the average per group and test if the gap is real.
